headline: MINRES TO RESTART BALD HILL LITHIUM MINE AFTER 18-MONTH SHUTDOWN — SITE MOBILISATION BEGINS LATE MAY
snippet: Mineral Resources (ASX: MIN) announced the restart of its Bald Hill hard rock lithium mine in Western Australia, with site mobilisation and workforce deployment beginning in late May 2026; the 165,000-tonne-per-annum spodumene operation was suspended 18 months ago during the lithium price collapse, and first production is targeted for July with first shipment in Q1 FY2027. The restart costs approximately A$20 million and makes MinRes the only company globally running three operating hard rock lithium mines.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE DROPS FROM 2-YEAR HIGH AS MINE RESTARTS SIGNAL SUPPLY RESPONSE TO $200K/T PRICES
snippet: Lithium carbonate fell to CNY 178,000/t on May 22, retreating from the two-year high of CNY 200,500 set on May 13 as surging prices prompted rapid supply-side response including the MinRes Bald Hill restart; Chinese EV output rose 5.5% year-on-year to 1.32 million units in the latest month while sales climbed 9.7% to 1.34 million, confirming the demand picture that drove prices to their highest in nearly three years.

headline: COBALT UP 67% YEAR-ON-YEAR AT $56,290/T AS DRC HOPES CLASH WITH RISING INDONESIA SUPPLY RISK
snippet: Cobalt held near $56,290/t in May 2026 — up 67% year-on-year — as the market navigates contradictory supply signals: improving DRC output availability is being offset by fresh supply risks in Indonesia; the battery metal's sharp recovery from 2024 lows has revived capital flows to junior cobalt developers, with May's monthly digest tracking exploration activity and equity moves across the sector.

headline: NICKEL CLIMBS ABOVE $18,800 AS INDONESIA'S WEDA BAY INDUSTRIAL PARK TRIMS UP TO 15% OF NPI OUTPUT
snippet: Nickel recovered to $18,880/t on May 22, up 21.3% year-on-year, bouncing from a four-week low of $18,555 hit on May 18; 10-15% of high-grade nickel pig iron capacity at Weda Bay Industrial Park in Indonesia is undergoing rotational maintenance in coming months, tightening spot availability at a time when Western EV battery supply chains are accelerating procurement of battery-grade nickel outside China.

headline: CHINA IMPORTED 790+ TONNES OF SILVER IN EARLY 2026 — SOLAR PANEL BOOM IS REWIRING GLOBAL DEMAND
snippet: China's silver imports exceeded 790 tonnes in early 2026 with solar panel manufacturing cited as the dominant driver, the latest Gold SWOT analysis reveals; this structural industrial demand — tied to energy transition capex rather than investor sentiment — provides a demand floor that fundamentally distinguishes the current silver bull market from the 2011 speculative spike, which collapsed when ETF flows reversed and left no physical demand to support prices.

headline: GOLD BREAKS BELOW ALL THREE KEY MOVING AVERAGES — CHART FLAGS $4,250 SUPPORT AS NEXT DOWNSIDE TARGET
snippet: With gold trading near $4,509 on May 24, the metal has broken below its 21-DMA ($4,624), 50-DMA ($4,670), and 100-DMA ($4,800) simultaneously — a technically bearish configuration last seen in the mid-2024 correction; the next major support is the rising 200-DMA near $4,250, and analysts note that COMEX open interest has stagnated for weeks, suggesting the move lower is driven by disengagement rather than aggressive selling — which can reverse sharply on a catalyst.

headline: JPMORGAN SLASHES 2026 GOLD AVERAGE TO $5,243 AS INSTITUTIONAL DEMAND "DRIES TO A TRICKLE"
snippet: JPMorgan cut its full-year 2026 gold average price forecast to $5,243/oz from $5,708, citing COMEX open interest at multi-month lows, anemic ETF inflows, and institutional client interest that has "dried to a trickle"; the bank also trimmed its central bank purchase estimate to 640 tonnes and ETF inflow forecast to 400 tonnes for full-year 2026 — but kept a bullish $6,000/oz year-end target, expecting H2 demand to recover sharply as macro tailwinds reassert.

headline: SILVER MAY 2026 OUTLOOK: STOP CHASING THE RALLY — THE STRUCTURAL DEFICIT CASE IS WHAT MATTERS
snippet: Contrarian analysis argues investors should stop chasing silver's volatile intraday swings and focus on the structural thesis: silver hit an all-time high of $121.64 in January, gave back most gains through April consolidation, then surged 6% in a single session on May 11 after US-China tariff reduction news — that kind of explosive response to positive catalysts is the hallmark of a bull market in a structural deficit, not a distribution phase preparing for a top.

headline: GOLDSEEK WEEKLY #72: GOLD, SILVER AND MINERS ALL WAITING FOR THE SAME CATALYST TO BREAK THE RANGE
snippet: GoldSeek's Issue #72 weekly digest finds precious metals and mining equities in a synchronized consolidation below their Q1 highs, with both institutional and retail investors asking what specific macro catalyst breaks the range; the digest examines whether the US-Iran oil price shock, the next Federal Reserve meeting, or a resumption of central bank gold buying is most likely to serve as the trigger — and which mining sub-sectors are showing the earliest accumulation signals ahead of the next leg.

headline: BARRICK CEO HINTS AT EARLY FOURMILE AGREEMENT WITH NEWMONT AS NEVADA LEGAL BATTLE ENTERS HEARINGS
snippet: Barrick Mining CEO Mark Hill said the company may reach an early agreement with Newmont over the Fourmile gold discovery — one of the world's highest-grade undeveloped gold deposits — as both majors head into preliminary hearings over Newmont's "resource piracy" allegations within the Nevada Gold Mines joint venture; any Fourmile resolution would materially de-risk Barrick's planned North American spinoff, which also requires Newmont's formal consent to proceed under the joint venture agreement.

headline: KAZAKH SUPPLY SURGE TESTS URANIUM'S MOMENTUM — BUT STRUCTURAL BULL CASE IS INTACT BENEATH THE NOISE
snippet: Analysis argues Kazatomprom's expanded output has temporarily weighed on uranium spot ($84.70/lb) but that the structural underpinning remains intact: 70 new reactors under construction globally, chronic utility under-contracting that leaves buyers exposed, and Kazatomprom's own stated preference for value over volume — the world's lowest-cost producer has reiterated it will not aggressively ramp output at current prices, limiting how far spot can fall before producer discipline reasserts.

headline: WHEATON PRECIOUS METALS POSTS Q1 RECORDS AND CLOSES LARGEST STREAMING DEAL IN COMPANY HISTORY
snippet: Wheaton Precious Metals (TSX: WPM) reported record Q1 2026 revenue, earnings, and cash flow on the back of outperformance at its Salobo and Peñasquito streams, while simultaneously closing its largest-ever streaming transaction at the Antamina copper-silver mine in Peru and entering its first Australian streaming agreement via KGL Resources; the results underscore how streamers are capturing the full benefit of elevated commodity prices without bearing the operational cost inflation that has squeezed conventional producers this cycle.
